sum: This study investigates strong ground motion attenuation in the Sichuan basin using dense records from ten moderate-to-large earthquakes. It reveals a slower attenuation rate and a plateau between 80–160 km source distances, attributed to constructive interference between direct waves and post-critical Moho reflections. The basin exhibits lower anelastic attenuation and smaller within-event variability compared to surrounding regions, linked to its homogeneous crustal structure. The authors propose a novel four-segment geometric attenuation function with specific breakpoints, offering a statistically superior fit and better capturing far-field attenuation characteristics than conventional models. This work has significant implications for ground-motion modeling and seismic hazard assessment in the region.

sum: This study presents a 3D numerical model of the Farallon plate subduction and fragmentation beneath southwestern North America from 60 Ma to the present. By incorporating reconstructed plate kinematics and seafloor age as boundary conditions, the model successfully predicts a slab geometry that matches high P-wave velocity anomalies in the upper mantle. The results show that subduction waned between 40 and 30 Ma, leading to slab thinning, flattening, and a first detachment at ~26 Ma. The subsequent propagation of a slab window facilitated asthenospheric upwelling and decompression melting, showing a strong spatial and temporal correlation with regional mafic volcanic occurrences in northwestern Mexico and the southwestern United States.

sum: This paper presents a unified framework for causal and uncertainty-aware instrument correction in broadband seismology. Instead of using heuristic stabilization, the author formulates deconvolution as a constrained inverse problem in the digital domain. The method enforces causal realizability and bounded inverse behavior while introducing regularization to control the bias-noise trade-off. It quantifies discretization effects that cause systematic amplitude bias and propagates parametric instrument uncertainties to derive confidence bounds on amplitude response and noise amplification. A data-driven decision framework with diagnostic metrics is introduced to objectively select the inverse filter and define the reliable frequency range.
本文提出了一种用于宽频带地震学中因果与不确定性感知仪器校正的统一框架。作者将反褶积公式化为数字域中的约束反问题，而非采用启发式稳定方法。该方法在引入正则化以控制偏差-噪声权衡的同时，确保了因果可实现性和有界反向行为。它量化了导致系统振幅偏差的离散化效应，并传播参数化仪器不确定性以推导振幅响应和噪声放……

sum: This study presents a new 3D lithospheric-scale resistivity model of the Miocene-Recent Malawi rift, Africa, to investigate the roles of magmatic modification and pre-rift structural heterogeneity on early-stage rifting. The magnetotelluric imaging reveals low-resistivity zones beneath the Rungwe Volcanic Province, interpreted as magma storage in the crust (8-20 km depth) and mantle-lithosphere (30-70 km depth). It also identifies highly resistive Proterozoic orogenic terranes bounded by linear conductive belts at lower-crustal and upper-mantle depths, likely representing graphite-bearing suture zones. The results show that Malawi rift border faults mostly cross-cut, rather than follow, these ancient suture zones.

sum: This paper proposes the Tripartite Spatiotemporal Triggering Hypothesis (TSTH) to explain remote earthquake triggering beyond traditional near-field limits. TSTH categorizes far-field effects into three mechanisms: Antipodal Resonance (~20,000 km, days-to-months lag), Plate-Margin Symmetric-End Stress Transfer (>5,000 km, 1-3 years lag), and Conventional Plate-Margin Compressional Transfer. The hypothesis is validated using historical cases (2010 Chile Mw8.8, 2023 Turkey Mw7.8) and real-time tracking of a 2026 global sequence. Monte Carlo simulations (10,000 runs) demonstrate that the observed spatiotemporal clustering is highly statistically significant (p < 1e-5), suggesting a physical basis for cross-scale remote triggering.

sum: This paper presents a Bayesian geometry-based gravity inversion framework designed for stratigraphic reconstruction. To overcome the limited vertical resolution and strong non-uniqueness of gravity data, the authors parameterize stratigraphic interfaces using a compact Fourier series. This parameterization enables a controllable representation of layer geometry and improves vertical resolution. Uncertainty in the inferred stratigraphy is quantified using Stein variational inference (SVI), which provides an ensemble approximation of the posterior distribution. The method is validated on two toy examples, two synthetic lunar basin models representing alternative crustal layering hypotheses, and real satellite gravity observations from the Orientale Basin on the Moon, successfully recovering its large-scale tectonic structure.
本文提出了一种用于地层重建的贝叶斯几何重力反演框架。为解决重力反演多解性强和纵向分辨率低的问题，研究采用傅里叶级数对地层界面进行参数化，实现了对地层几何形态的紧凑且可控表征。利用斯坦变分推断（SVI）进行不确定性量化，获得后验分布的集合逼近。该方法在两个简单示例、两个月球盆地合成模型以及月球东海盆地……

sum: This study investigates why near-seafloor marine sediments on active margins are stronger than those on passive margins. The authors performed resedimentation and oedometer tests to measure undrained shear strength, grain size, mineralogy, and plasticity on sediments from three active margins (Nankai, Cascadia, Surveyor Fan) and three passive margins (Amazon Fan, Carolina, New Jersey), comparing them to in situ field measurements. While resedimented samples fall within normal consolidation ranges, in situ Nankai and Cascadia sediments show anomalously high shear strength and low porosity. The results suggest that repeated exposure to earthquakes and lateral shear strain from non-uniaxial stress paths are required to explain this elevated strength.
本研究探讨了为何活动边缘的近海底沉积物强度高于被动边缘。作者对三个活动边缘（南海、卡斯卡迪亚、测量员扇）和三个被动边缘（亚马逊扇、卡罗莱纳、新泽西）的沉积物进行了重塑和固结实验，测量了无排水剪切强度、粒径、矿物学和塑性，并与原位测量进行了对比。结果显示，重塑样品的剪切强度均处于正常固结范围内，但南海……

t: Resedimentation and oedometer testing combined with laboratory measurements of undrained shear strength, grain size, mineralogy, and plasticity to characterize sediment consolidation behavior.
采用重塑和固结仪试验，结合无排水剪切强度、粒径、矿物学和塑性的实验室测量。
Sediment samples and in situ measurements from three active margins (Nankai, Cascadia, Surveyor Fan) and three passive margins (Amazon Fan, Carolina, New Jersey).
来自三个活动边缘（南海、卡斯卡迪亚、测量员扇）和三个被动边缘的沉积物样品及原位数据。
Resedimented samples show normal consolidation, but in situ Nankai and Cascadia sediments exhibit anomalously high shear strength and low porosity that 1-D consolidation cannot reproduce.
重塑样品呈正常固结，但南海和卡斯卡迪亚原位样品具有一维固结无法解释的高强度和低孔隙度。
Standard 1-D consolidation experiments fail to capture the complex non-uniaxial stress paths and dynamic earthquake history experienced by active margin sediments.

Directly proves that intrinsic sediment properties and normal consolidation are insufficient to explain active margin sediment strength, requiring dynamic tectonic and seismic processes.
直接证明了沉积物固有属性和正常固结不足以解释活动边缘强度，必须引入动态构造与地震过程。

Compared physical and mechanical properties of sediments across three active and three passive margins using both laboratory experiments and field data.

sum: This study presents a hybrid, semi-automated framework to systematically identify previously undocumented submarine calderas globally. Utilizing the low-resolution but globally available General Bathymetric Chart of the Oceans (GEBCO) dataset, the authors combine an automated depression-detection algorithm (originally adapted from planetary crater detection) with expert user classification and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) validation. The framework successfully identified 78 calderas spanning diverse tectonic settings and depths up to 5,600 m, of which 73 were previously undocumented. A sensitivity analysis reveals that under-detection is primarily linked to low circularity indexes (< 50%). This work fills a critical observational gap in marine volcanology and provides an upgradeable, reproducible tool for global volcanic hazard assessment.
本研究提出了一种半自动混合框架，用于在全球范围内系统识别未被记录的海底破火山口。该方法利用全球低分辨率GEBCO水深数据，结合自动地形洼地检测算法、专家人工分类以及主成分分析（PCA）验证。该框架成功识别出78个破火山口（水深可达5600米），其中73个为首次发现。敏感性测试表明，漏检主要与低圆形度……

sum: This study evaluates historical earthquake recurrence patterns along the Dead Sea transform (DST) by integrating instrumental, historical, archaeological, and paleoseismic datasets spanning the past ~2000 years. The authors compile destructive earthquakes and analyze their magnitude distribution alongside ~40 years of microseismicity. They find that M >= 7.0 earthquakes occur more frequently than predicted by the Gutenberg-Richter relation, while M 6.0-6.9 events are relatively scarce. This supports a characteristic earthquake model. However, several exceptionally large historical events (e.g., 749, 1202, 1759 C.E.) suggest a bimodal or multimodal distribution. The paper concludes that M 7.0-7.3 earthquakes are most characteristic of the DST, with less frequent M 7.4-8.0 events, reconciling the debate on characteristic earthquake behavior and improving regional seismic hazard assessments.

sum: This paper investigates the spatial and temporal evolution of stress changes in the Longmenshan fault zone and its surrounding regions following the devastating 2008 MW7.9 Wenchuan earthquake. By modeling static and viscoelastic stress transfer, the study evaluates how the mainshock redistributed stress on neighboring fault segments, influencing subsequent seismicity and regional seismic hazards. The findings provide critical insights into fault interactions and earthquake triggering mechanisms in active continental collision zones.
本研究探讨了2008年MW7.9汶川大地震后龙门山断裂带及周边地区应力变化的空时演化。通过模拟库仑应力变化和粘弹性应力松弛，评估了主震对邻近断层段的应力再分配，及其对后续地震活动性和区域地震危险性的影响。研究结果为活动大陆碰撞带的断层相互作用和地震触发机制提供了关键见解。

sum: This study models earthquake populations propagating and arresting within a stochastic stress field using a 1D fracture mechanics framework. The authors show that realistic earthquake populations (with Gutenberg-Richter-like scaling) are produced when the standard deviation of the potential stress drop far exceeds its mean, creating significant sections of highly negative potential stress. The resulting earthquake populations exhibit b-values that decrease with increasing mean stress, and magnitude-independent stress drops. The preferred scaling exponent (0 to 0.25) suggests highly variable stress even at short wavelengths, consistent with exhumed fault roughness.
本研究利用一维断裂力学框架，模拟了地震在随机应力场中的传播与停止。结果表明，当潜在应力降的标准差远大于其平均值（导致出现显著的负应力降区域）时，能够产生符合实际观测的地震序列。模拟得到的b值随平均应力增加而减小，且应力降与震级无关。优选的标度指数（0至0.25）表明短波长下应力具有极高变异性，这与露……

sum: This study analyzes 30 three-component strong-motion recordings from Myanmar and Thailand to quantify the regional ground-motion characteristics of the 2025 Mw 7.7 Mandalay earthquake. By calculating amplitude and duration residuals relative to NGA-West2 models, the authors identify a pronounced azimuthal directivity pattern. Stations aligned with the Mach fronts of the southward-propagating supershear rupture (110–155 degrees azimuth) exhibit large positive spectral acceleration residuals and strongly negative D5–95 duration residuals. Conversely, stations to the southwest and west show negative amplitude and positive duration residuals. This bilateral contrast matches the expected Mach cone radiation pattern, demonstrating that supershear rupture effects persist into the far-field (150–600 km) and should be incorporated into seismic hazard assessments for large strike-slip faults.

sum: This study presents a novel wavefield-based earthquake localization method designed for distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) systems. To overcome the single-component directional sensitivity of DAS, the authors use full-waveform simulations in heterogeneous velocity models to generate synthetic DAS wavefield images. A deep convolutional neural network (CNN) based on a U-Net architecture is trained on these images to map wavefield patterns directly to earthquake source coordinates, bypassing the need for manual or automated P- and S-wave arrival picking. Tested on a challenging synthetic case study of a single vertical borehole, the CNN successfully learns location-specific wavefield signatures. The study demonstrates that localization uncertainties can be significantly reduced by incorporating data from a second borehole, offering a promising tool for microseismic monitoring.

sum: This paper introduces a novel characterization of seismic site response called the time-frequency transfer function, TFTF(t, f). While the standard Fourier transfer function (FTF) only provides frequency-domain amplification and resonance peaks, it lacks temporal resolution. The proposed TFTF(t, f) overcomes this limitation by tracking the temporal development of the frequency content of the transfer function. The authors present the underlying theory and demonstrate its application to quasi-1D canonical models of local sedimentary structures. In a semi-infinite layer model, TFTF successfully distinguishes vertical resonance modes from surface wave modes, a task that is impossible using standard FTF.

sum: This study applies multi-scale wavelet decomposition to high-resolution residual gravity anomalies in the Tangshan seismic zone to isolate crustal structure signals across different depth ranges. By integrating these structural signatures with spatial seismicity, the authors characterize the tectonic framework of the Tangshan rhombic fault block within the North China Craton. Shallow anomalies (1st-3rd orders) reflect Quaternary sedimentary layers and diffuse shallow seismicity, while intermediate anomalies (4th-7th orders) delineate the rhombic block and bounding faults hosting the mainshock. Deep anomalies (8th-10th orders) image mantle upwelling and density heterogeneities, suggesting that upward thermal ascent induces lower crustal weakening and stress transfer to shallower locked faults, driving intense stress accumulation.

sum: This study investigates lithospheric thinning and deformation decoupling beneath the East African Rift System (EARS) using a high-resolution seismic tomography model of Africa combined with active- and passive-source seismic compilations. By estimating mantle temperatures, the lithosphere-asthenosphere boundary, and crustal thickness, the authors calculate thinning factors for both the crust and lithospheric mantle. They find that while the magma-rich eastern branch exhibits coupled crust-mantle thinning, the magma-poor western branch shows complex, decoupled thinning. The results suggest that lithospheric mantle necking precedes crustal necking during continental rifting, influenced by structural inheritance, lithospheric delamination, and melt-induced ductile strain.

sum: This study presents a systematic investigation of tectonic tremor tidal sensitivity along the northeastern Japan subduction zone using a tremor catalog from 2016 to 2024. The authors find that the southern end of the Kuril Trench, characterized by tremor migration and weak seismicity, exhibits the strongest tidal sensitivity, whereas the northern Japan Trench shows the weakest. Areas with weaker tidal sensitivity coincide with higher earthquake rates and denser tremor activity. Additionally, tidal sensitivity increases during the progression of tremor migration, indicating modulation by underlying slow slip processes. These findings suggest that tremor tidal sensitivity serves as a diagnostic probe for the local stress perturbation environment.

sum: This paper introduces GeoRisk-MLLM, a multimodal large language model framework designed for natural disaster risk detection and early warning in geosciences, including earthquakes and landslides. The framework integrates remote sensing imagery, temporal monitoring data, and IoT sensor streams using a hierarchical Transformer architecture with contrastive learning. It aligns visual features with reasoning processes to generate interpretable risk assessment reports and utilizes KV cache compression and knowledge distillation for efficient edge deployment. Evaluated on three geoscience benchmark datasets, GeoRisk-MLLM achieves an average AUC of 0.934, demonstrating superior performance, generalization, and interpretability compared to existing methods.

sum: This paper presents an overview of the SEIS-ADELICE project (2020–2025), which deployed hundreds of seismological instruments (broadband, mid-band, and short-period) on land and at sea around the Astrolabe Coastal Glacier in East Antarctica. The primary objective is to monitor cryoseismic activity, image internal glacier structure, and investigate interactions between the glacier, ocean, and bedrock. The authors describe the sequential deployment phases, analyze seismic noise levels across various environments, and evaluate data quality across different frequency bands. Non-exhaustive data examples demonstrate the dataset's high quality and its potential for analyzing diverse cryoseismic sources across multiple spatial and temporal scales.
本文介绍了SEIS-ADELICE项目（2020-2025）的观测成果。该项目在东南极阿斯特罗拉布冰川及其周边陆地和海洋部署了数百台宽频带、中频带和短周期地震仪。研究旨在监测冰震活动、成像冰川内部结构与厚度，并探究冰川与底层海洋及局部基岩的相互作用。文中详细描述了仪器的分阶段部署、不同环境下的噪声水……

展示了高质量的多频段地震数据，能够有效解析多种冰震源并表征极地环境噪声特征。
The study is primarily observational and descriptive, focusing on instrumentation, noise levels, and data quality rather than detailed physical modeling.

sum: This paper develops a theoretical framework for lunar tides in a coupled Earth core and basal magma ocean (BMO) system. Unlike traditional models where tidal forces deform the outer boundary, this model focuses on the tidal potential acting directly on the density contrast at the core-BMO interface. In the inviscid limit, the system transitions from an equilibrium tide to an inertia-self-gravity wave, with a resonance occurring when the forcing frequency matches the natural frequency of the interfacial mode. Incorporating finite viscosity regularizes this resonance and introduces phase lags. When integrated with lunar recession and BMO crystallization models, the theory predicts enhanced core-boundary ellipticity and core-flow speeds, offering a novel, tidally driven mechanism to power the early geodynamo prior to inner-core growth.
本文建立了地球核心与基底岩浆洋（BMO）耦合系统中的月球潮汐理论框架。与传统通过外边界形变传递潮汐力的方法不同，该模型聚焦于潮汐势直接作用于核-BMO界面的密度差。在无粘性极限下，系统随强迫频率增加从平衡潮过渡到惯性-自重力波，并在强迫频率匹配界面模式固有频率时发生共振。引入有限粘性可使共振正则化并……

对由密度界面分隔的双层流体系统（地核与基底岩浆洋）在潮汐力作用下的动力学进行理论建模，结合了无粘性极限与有限粘性边界层分…
Synthetic parameterizations and evolutionary models of early Earth-Moon orbital dynamics, lunar recession, and basal magma ocean crystallization history.

确定了一个共振区间，当潮汐强迫频率与界面模式的固有频率匹配时，会导致核流显著增强。
将无粘性核流解与经典的椭圆涡旋及椭圆不稳定理论联系起来。
证明了基底岩浆洋能显著增强与地核的潮汐耦合，为早期地磁发电机提供了一种可行的能量来源。

Inviscid and viscous boundary layer analysis of the interfacial wave response.
Integration with parameterized evolutionary models of lunar recession and basal magma ocean crystallization.
潮汐势下双层不混溶流体（液态金属核与基底岩浆洋）的理论流体动力学建模。
界面波响应的无粘性与有粘性边界层分析。

sum: This study utilizes a newly densified and improved GNSS velocity field of the western Aegean region to quantify slip rates, strain localization, and interseismic loading in central and southwestern Greece. The authors analyze four extensional regions and three strike-slip systems. Key findings show that the Corinth Rift accommodates westward-increasing extension (7 to 15 mm/yr) via combined elastic loading and aseismic creep on limited faults. In contrast, the Evia-Boeotia sector and southern Peloponnese exhibit diffuse deformation distributed across multiple structures. Strike-slip systems show contrasting behaviors: the Katouna segment undergoes rapid transtensional creep, while the Movri Fault remains locked down to 10 km depth. This work provides high-resolution geodetic constraints on the transition from subduction to collision.
本研究利用爱琴海西部地区加密和改进的GNSS速度场，定量分析了希腊中部和西南部的断层滑动速率、应变局域化及地震间期加载。研究涵盖四个伸展区和三个走滑系统。结果表明，科林斯裂谷NS向伸展向西从7增至15 mm/yr，由少数地壳级断层的弹性加载和无震蠕滑共同分担；而埃维亚和伯罗奔尼撒南部则表现为多条结构……

A new, improved, and densified GNSS velocity field covering active tectonic domains in central and southwestern Greece.

sum: This study investigates the structural and compositional modification of the lunar crust and mantle within the South Pole-Aitken (SPA) basin, the largest and oldest impact structure on the Moon. By analyzing the geodynamic and petrological evolution of this region, the authors shed light on how giant impacts reshape planetary lithospheres and redistribute mantle materials, providing critical insights into early lunar differentiation and subsequent magmatic processes.
本研究探讨了月球上最大、最古老的撞击构造——南极-艾特肯（SPA）盆地内月壳和月幔的结构与成分改造。通过分析该区域的地球动力学和岩石学演化，作者揭示了巨型撞击如何重塑行星岩石圈并重新分配地幔物质，为早期月球分异及随后的岩浆活动提供了关键见解。

sum: This study presents geochemical and isotopic data for hydrothermal gases from the southeastern Tibetan Plateau, including the Changning–Menglian suture (CMS), Tengchong volcanic field (TCV), and Red River fault zone (RRF). The authors identify distinct regional contrasts in hydrogen (H2) concentrations and origins. In the CMS, active H2 seepage is driven by the serpentinization of remnant oceanic lithosphere. In the TCV, magmatic degassing dominates, whereas fault-related processes and radiolysis prevail in the RRF. Tectonic activity and lithospheric deformation drive H2 release, with faults acting as conduits. Secondary processes during ascent, such as calcite precipitation and CO2 dissolution, further enrich H2, forming N2-rich and H2-bearing fluids. These findings provide critical insights into the tectonic controls on natural hydrogen generation and migration in active continental collision zones.

sum: This study presents the first rigorous experimental validation of seismic resonant metamaterials (metabarriers) for structural protection against vertically propagating horizontal seismic shear waves. Two dynamic centrifuge model tests were conducted at 50 g to compare an unprotected structure with one protected by 3D-printed unit-cell resonant metamaterials embedded in dense Hostun sand. The unit cells, tuned to 150 Hz (close to the structure's 160 Hz fixed-base frequency), significantly reduced structural and near-field accelerations at resonance. Digital image correlation (DIC) revealed that the protective mechanism is driven by the out-of-phase vibration of the unit-cell internal masses relative to the surrounding soil.

sum: This paper introduces RT-EDAP (Real-Time Event-Driven Data Aggregation and Processing), a novel framework designed to enhance tsunami early warning systems (TEWS). To address latency and scalability challenges, RT-EDAP utilizes edge computing and stream processing frameworks (Apache Kafka and Apache Flink) to process multi-source data streams (seismic, tide gauge, GPS) locally. It integrates lightweight edge models with centralized Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) for event classification. The system achieves 95% prediction accuracy and a low processing latency of 50-60ms, outperforming traditional centralized methods.

sum: This study employs physics-based ground-motion simulation on a supercomputer to re-evaluate seismic hazard for Hualien, Taiwan, a highly vulnerable region. It simulates four historical earthquakes (Mw 6.4-7.3) up to 8 Hz, incorporating realistic 3D velocity, topography, bathymetry, and calibrated finite-fault slip models. Waveform comparisons validate the simulations. The research investigates directivity effects by varying hypocenter locations and explores source modeling uncertainties with multiple finite-fault models. Results show physics-based simulations can exceed empirical ground-motion model predictions, highlighting significant site amplifications. The generated synthetic ground-motion database is valuable for seismic hazard and risk analysis in the Hualien area, offering a novel, high-frequency dataset.

sum: This study analyzes temperature data from over 3,000 nodal seismometers deployed in North Yorkshire during the July 2022 heatwave. The seismometers' embedded microcontroller sensors provided unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution, logging over 80 million temperature readings. Statistical corrections were applied using co-located meteorological data to account for sensor housing biases. The corrected dataset reveals significant microscale surface temperature heterogeneity, with mean differences up to 3.6°C over 100-200m and extreme contrasts exceeding 17°C. Variability was strongly modulated by meteorological forcing, with daytime heatwaves showing the most heterogeneity. Land-use classes showed modest differences. The findings highlight the importance of sub-kilometer temperature variability and the potential of repurposing geophysical arrays for microclimate characterization.

sum: This study investigates the kinematic behavior and structural segmentation of the East Anatolian Fault System (EAFS) and the Sürgü-Çardak Fault (SCF) following the devastating 2023 earthquakes. By integrating SBAS-InSAR surface displacement measurements from Sentinel-1A (2018–2023) with gravity-based subsurface structural mapping, the authors analyze deformation patterns across 14 profiles. The results reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity, indicating coexisting locked and creeping segments, and suggest that the 2023 mainshock nucleated in a highly locked, high-stress zone. Combining geodetic and gravity gradient data, they propose a revised five-segment structural framework for the EAFS, enhancing our understanding of fault architecture and seismic hazards.

sum: This study establishes a causal link between seamount subduction and giant gold mineralization. By analyzing gold contents in mafic rocks of varying metamorphic grades from accretionary complexes, the authors show that plume-modified samples have higher gold contents, which decrease during metamorphism. They propose a three-step genetic model: first, a mantle plume enriches seamounts with gold; second, subduction of these seamounts releases and stores gold at the base of the overriding plate; third, magmatic flare-ups and fluid activity transport the gold to the shallow crust. This model successfully explains the global correlation between gold deposits and subducted seamounts over the past 600 million years, providing a novel geodynamic framework for ore deposit exploration.
本研究确立了海山俯冲与巨型金矿成矿之间的因果联系。通过分析增生杂岩中不同变质程度基性岩的金含量，研究发现受地幔柱改造的样品金含量更高，且金含量在变质作用过程中降低。据此，研究提出一个三阶段成矿模型：地幔柱将深部地幔的金注入海山；海山链俯冲将金释放并储存在上覆板块底部；岩浆大爆发期间的流体活动将金运移……

sum: This study presents high-resolution seismic images of the mantle transition zone near Eurasia's northeastern margin, revealing a 700-km-deep discontinuity within the stagnant slab and a depressed 660-km discontinuity. The 700-km discontinuity matches the akimotoite-to-bridgmanite transition in an anhydrous basaltic assemblage, while the depressed 660-km discontinuity is likely water-induced. Combined with mineral physics modeling, the authors demonstrate that slab stagnation is initiated and sustained by buoyancy from excess depressions in the pyrolite and harzburgite mantle, assisted by the buoyancy of a dry basaltic assemblage in the uppermost lower mantle. This provides key insights into the thermodynamic and chemical mechanisms governing slab dynamics in the transition zone.

sum: This study analyzes long-period teleseismic P-wave polarization anomalies across Australia to constrain lateral velocity gradients and azimuthal anisotropy. Using a Bayesian harmonic analysis, the authors separate the phi-term (lateral heterogeneity) and 2-phi-term (azimuthal anisotropy). The positive velocity gradients correlate with crustal thinning along continental margins and localized lithosphere-asthenosphere boundary (LAB) variations. The fast-axis directions reveal tectonic-province-dependent variations: eastern Australia and the southern North Australian Craton reflect present-day asthenospheric mantle flow, whereas cratonic Australia preserves fossil lithospheric anisotropy. This demonstrates the utility of P-wave polarization as a complementary tool for continental-scale upper-mantle imaging.

sum: This study investigates the crustal-scale heterogeneity and seismic anisotropy across the Bhutan Himalayas using shear-wave splitting analysis of local earthquake waveforms. By analyzing the fast polarization directions (FPD) and delay times of split shear waves, the authors characterize the upper crustal stress field and structural fabric. The results reveal complex anisotropic patterns that correlate with major tectonic features such as the Main Central Thrust (MCT) and local fault systems. This work provides new insights into the deformation mechanisms, stress state, and crustal heterogeneity in the eastern Himalayan arc, highlighting the role of structural inheritance and active tectonics in shaping the region's crustal architecture.

sum: This study utilizes a high-resolution dense array catalog to investigate the Qiaojia-Dongchuan seismic gap near a major hydropower station. The authors reveal a vertical decoupling mechanism: shallow seismicity (high b-value of ~1.0) is driven by reservoir fluid triggering, whereas deep seismicity (~20 km, low b-value <0.8) indicates a locked tectonic asperity with high Coulomb stress accumulation. This suggests the seismic gap is in a critical state with high rupture potential, and warns that shallow induced seismicity can mask deep tectonic strain accumulation.
本研究利用密集台阵地震目录分析巧家-东川地震空区。研究揭示了垂直解耦机制：浅层地震b值高（~1.0），为流体驱动的水库触发地震；深部地震（~20 km）b值低（<0.8）且库仑应力积累率高，表明存在锁定微凸体。这表明该空区处于高破裂潜能的临界状态，并警示浅层诱发地震会掩盖深部构造应力的无声积累。

t: The study utilizes a high-resolution dense array catalog to analyze spatial variations in b-values and model Coulomb stress accumulation rates.

sum: This paper presents a fault-wide paleoseismic reconstruction of the Eskişehir Fault in northwestern Central Anatolia, Türkiye. By analyzing geological and paleoseismic evidence, the authors identify a mature, late-cycle seismic gap along this fault system. They evaluate the rupture potential and seismic hazard associated with this structure, providing critical constraints on future earthquake scenarios in this active tectonic region.

sum: This study develops a geospatial site amplification model for the Basin and Range Province of the western United States using 16,852 recordings from 433 stations in the NGA-West3 database. The base model uses mapped geospatial variables (sediment thickness, elevation, surficial geology) in a linear mixed-effects regression to predict site amplification residuals from the BSSA14 ground-motion model. This base model achieves an average 8.5% reduction in site-to-site variability. The model is further enhanced with local geotechnical data, including microtremor horizontal-to-vertical spectral ratio (mHVSR) and measured VS30 data, yielding additional variability reductions. This framework demonstrates how combining regional geospatial data with sparse site-specific geotechnical measurements can effectively characterize site amplification and uncertainty in data-sparse regions.

sum: floatCSEP is a Python-based software package developed to facilitate reproducible prospective earthquake forecasting experiments. As part of the Collaboratory for the Study of Earthquake Predictability (CSEP), floatCSEP automates the workflow of retrieving earthquake catalogs, running forecasting models (such as ETAS), and performing statistical evaluations (e.g., N-test, S-test). It provides a standardized, containerized, or local environment to ensure that forecasting experiments are fully reproducible, transparent, and easily deployable by the seismological community.

sum: This study evaluates the performance of two real-time earthquake localization algorithms, RTLoc and MParLoc, within the QuakeUp Earthquake Early Warning System (EEWS) for the Ibero-Maghrebian Region (IMR). Using Mw >= 4 earthquakes from 2011 to 2026, the authors demonstrate that MParLoc, which integrates P-wave arrival times, P-peak amplitude ratios, and back-azimuth estimates, significantly outperforms RTLoc. MParLoc provides more accurate hypocentral locations during the critical early stages of detection when data is sparse. This early-stage precision reduces errors in ground motion prediction equations (GMPEs) and improves the delineation of Potential Damage Zones (PDZs), thereby enhancing the lead-time and reliability of real-time warnings.

sum: This study evaluates the "b-more-positive" estimator, which uses positive magnitude differences, to improve b-value estimation in regional seismic catalogs. Traditional estimators often underestimate the b-value due to spatial and temporal variations in catalog completeness. By testing on synthetic ETAS catalogs with simulated incompleteness and real instrumental catalogs from Japan, Italy, Southern California, Northern California, and New Zealand, the authors demonstrate that the b-more-positive method yields highly accurate and robust results. The findings suggest that conventional methods systematically underestimate regional b-values, which has significant implications for seismic hazard assessment and forecasting. Additionally, the method reveals genuine regional variations in b-values across different tectonic settings.

sum: This study constructs a high-resolution 3D P-wave velocity model of the upper mantle beneath the Pamir, Tianshan, and adjacent regions using teleseismic tomography from 353 stations and 3,321 events. The model reveals a subvertical boundary between the low-velocity central Tianshan and high-velocity Tarim lithosphere, indicating sub-horizontal compression and subsequent lithospheric delamination. In the Pamir-Hindu Kush region, the results show steep subduction of the Indian lithosphere beneath the Hindu Kush and sub-horizontal underthrusting beneath the Pamir, which likely triggers Tajik lithospheric delamination. Additionally, a large-scale high-velocity anomaly near the base of the mantle transition zone suggests detached Indian lithosphere from a ~20 Ma slab breakoff. These findings provide critical constraints on the deep mantle dynamics of the northwestern India-Asia collision zone.
本研究利用353个台站的远震数据，构建了帕米尔和天山地区上地幔三维P波速度模型。结果显示，塔里木岩石圈水平挤压天山并导致其拆沉；印度岩石圈在兴都库什陡峭俯冲，在帕米尔水平底辟并诱发塔吉克岩石圈拆沉；地幔过渡带底部的高速异常代表约20 Ma前断裂脱落的印度岩石圈。该研究揭示了西北印度-亚洲碰撞带的深部……

sum: This paper presents an adaptive local inverse-Hessian preconditioning approach for multiparameter elastic full-waveform inversion (FWI). Multiparameter elastic FWI often suffers from parameter coupling and unbalanced radiation sensitivities, leading to crosstalk and slow convergence. To address this, the authors construct a local inverse mapping between curvature responses (Hessian-vector products) and model perturbations using reference perturbations. This formulation captures both diagonal and off-diagonal inverse Hessian contributions, explicitly treating parameter coupling. The local systems are solved using singular value decomposition (SVD) with Tikhonov regularization. Synthetic tests, including a crosstalk-sensitive anomaly test and the Marmousi II model, demonstrate that the method produces update directions consistent with fully converged Gauss-Newton solutions at a fraction of the computational cost, outperforming block-diagonal pseudo-Hessian and truncated Gauss-Newton methods in crosstalk reduction and convergence speed.

sum: This study presents rapid UAV- and ground-based magnetic mapping to delineate subsurface fractures during the volcano-tectonic crisis in Grindavík, Iceland. By capturing high-resolution magnetic anomalies, the authors map the spatial distribution and orientation of active fractures and dyke-induced structures. This rapid deployment demonstrates the utility of aeromagnetic and ground magnetic surveys for real-time hazard assessment and structural characterization in active volcanic and rifting environments.

sum: This study simulates seismic wavefields for five moderate-to-large earthquakes in California to evaluate pseudospectral acceleration at periods of 2, 5, and 10 s. Using finite-difference calculations, the authors compare the USGS National Crustal Model with three established regional community velocity models (CVMS4.26.M01, CVMH15.1.0, and the USGS Bay Area CVM). The 3D models generally outperform ergodic ground-motion models. Crucially, the study demonstrates that averaging ground-motion predictions across all available velocity models yields better results than using any single model, suggesting that combining independent 3D velocity models can significantly improve seismic hazard and ground-motion estimations.

sum: This study investigates seismic wave amplification in the thick Cenozoic Gilan and Qazvin sedimentary basins of northern Iran (>10 km thick) to assess seismic hazards for multi-story buildings. Analyzing waveforms from 350 local earthquakes (72 stations) and teleseismic shear waves from 189 events, the authors find significant amplification at 0.8–5.0 Hz (peak factors >5 at ~1.0 Hz) and long periods (1–10 s). Horizontal-to-Vertical Spectral Ratio (HVSR) analysis of earthquakes and ambient noise demonstrates that this amplification is driven by deep sedimentary layers rather than shallow soil. The study provides the first quantitative assessment of low-frequency basin amplification in Iran, highlighting its linear behavior at large magnitudes and the critical need to incorporate these deep basin effects into regional seismic hazard models.

sum: This paper investigates the physical mechanism behind breakdown work scaling in laboratory earthquakes. Using experimental observations and theoretical analysis, the authors demonstrate that the observed scaling of breakdown work with slip or rupture propagation is not primarily a reflection of local frictional or fracture processes at the rupture tip. Instead, it is governed by nonlocal elastic unloading of the surrounding experimental apparatus or host rock system. This finding challenges traditional interpretations of seismological fracture energy and provides a new framework for scaling laboratory-derived earthquake parameters to natural fault systems.

sum: This study investigates the December 2019 earthquake crisis at the Condor Seamount, Azores, using rapid-response data from five ocean-bottom seismometers (OBS) deployed for three months. By applying a machine-learning-based phase picker, the authors construct a high-resolution earthquake catalog. Joint analysis with a long-term regional catalog reveals episodic, spatially stable seismicity in the uppermost mantle. The findings suggest the presence of an inflating magma reservoir beneath the seamount's tip that could feed future eruptions. This work highlights the value of rapid-response OBS deployments and machine learning in monitoring submarine volcanic systems.

sum: This study investigates three-dimensional seismo- and tsunami-traveling ionospheric disturbances (STIDs and TTIDs) triggered by the 29 July 2025 Mw8.8 Kamchatka earthquake. Using Doppler frequency shifts (DFSs) from continuous wave-high frequency Doppler sounding systems and ionograms from five ionosondes in Taiwan and Japan, the authors characterize the propagation dynamics. STIDs travel horizontally at supersonic speeds of 3.7 km/s (period ~20 s, wavelength ~74 km) and vertically upward at the speed of sound (period ~40 s, wavelength ~16 km). TTIDs, consisting of infrasonic and acoustic-gravity waves, travel horizontally near the tsunami speed (~200 m/s). Notably, the ionospheric disturbances in DFSs are tens of thousands of times larger than the ground-level vertical fluctuations of the seismic and tsunami waves, demonstrating the extreme amplification of acoustic-gravity waves in the upper atmosphere.

sum: This paper introduces EKI-MultiCMT, a novel framework for Multiple Centroid Moment Tensor (Multi-CMT) inversion of complex earthquakes. Traditional joint inversions using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) are computationally prohibitive, requiring over 10^5 forward simulations. EKI-MultiCMT leverages Ensemble Kalman Inversion (EKI), a derivative-free, ensemble-based optimization method, to update all subevent parameters collectively. The framework incorporates physical priors via Tikhonov regularization and augmented observations, including aftershock-derived kernel-density location estimates, cross-correlation similarity, and lag-time measurements. Using a randomize-then-optimize strategy, it generates an ensemble of solutions to characterize uncertainty. EKI-MultiCMT reduces the required forward simulations by two to three orders of magnitude compared to MCMC, making joint Multi-CMT inversion computationally feasible for complex, multi-segment rupture events.

sum: This study proposes a novel uniaxial compression testing method to investigate the macroscopic deformation and failure mechanisms of rock bridges under compressive-shear stress. By designing specimens with varying rock bridge angles, the authors successfully induced compressive-shear-dominated stress states. They integrated mechanical response analysis, acoustic emission (AE) monitoring, and digital image correlation (DIC) measurements to capture the failure process. The results show a characteristic valley-shaped AE activity evolution, with average frequency and rise angle parameters indicating shear-dominated cracking. DIC measurements revealed a circular vertical displacement field prior to failure, providing experimental evidence for circular slip surface formation in locked-type landslides. This work enhances the experimental characterization of rock bridge shear failure.

sum: This paper proposes the Unified Theory of Lithosphere-Atmosphere-Ionosphere Coupling via Acoustic-Gravity Waves (LAIC-AGW). Utilizing real-time time-series data (pressure, temperature, relative humidity) from an ultra-dense Netatmo IoT weather station array across Japan, the author monitors pre-seismic thermodynamic anomalies and post-seismic atmospheric wave propagation. By calculating equivalent potential temperature (\theta_e) via Bolton's equations, the study identifies a pre-seismic thermal spike (\Delta \theta_e = 27.99 K) hours before the M7.1 Kumamoto earthquake. Applying Continuous Wavelet Transform and delay-and-sum beamforming, the study validates the coupling theory across four major Japanese earthquakes, satisfying three pre-registered falsifiability gates (SNR, phase velocity, and focal radiation correlation). This work advances proactive earthquake risk management.

sum: This study presents high-resolution multichannel seismic (MCS) and ocean-bottom seismometer (OBS) data from the Danube Fan in the northwestern Black Sea to characterize its sedimentary structure, fluid migration, and slope stability. By deriving P- and S-wave velocity models, the authors identify under-consolidated, clay-rich levee deposits with low shear strength and high Vp/Vs ratios. Widespread vertical gas migration is evidenced by seismic chimneys, polarity reversals, and velocity pull-downs. Crucially, the lack of S-wave velocity anomalies suggests that gas hydrates exist as sparse, pore-filling accumulations rather than cementing agents, meaning they do not directly enhance sediment strength. Consequently, slope instability is primarily controlled by lithology, high sedimentation rates, and gas migration pathways rather than hydrate dynamics.
本研究利用黑海西北部多瑙河扇的高分辨率多道地震（MCS）和海底地震仪（OBS）数据，表征了其沉积结构、流体运移和斜坡稳定性。通过构建P波和S波速度模型，发现浅部存在低剪切强度和高Vp/Vs比的欠固结富粘土堤坝沉积。地震烟囱、极性反转和速度拉低表明存在广泛的垂直气体运移。关键是，S波速度异常的缺失表明……

sum: This Zenodo repository contains the model input files, geometry, frictional parameters, and simulated event catalogues (time, magnitude, location) associated with the paper 'Single Fault Earthquake Cycle Complexity' by Sun and Becker (2026). The simulations were conducted using the quasi-dynamic boundary element code HBI. The dataset includes a summary spreadsheet mapping each model run to its corresponding figure, frictional parameters, analysis window, and recurrence statistics, enabling full reproducibility of the study's findings on fault complexity.
该Zenodo存储库包含Sun和Becker（2026）发表的《单断层地震周期复杂性》论文相关的模型输入文件、几何形状、摩擦参数及模拟地震事件目录（时间、震级和位置）。模拟采用准动态边界元代码HBI进行。数据集还包括一个汇总电子表格，将每个模型运行与相应的图表、摩擦参数、分析窗口和复现统计数据进行映……

sum: This study investigates the 2009 L'Aquila seismic sequence to understand the mechanisms driving aftershock distribution. By analyzing the fault-zone architecture and seismicity patterns, the authors demonstrate that the spatial and temporal evolution of aftershocks is highly controlled by both the structural complexity of the fault zone and fluid migration processes. The findings highlight that seismicity patterns closely mirror the underlying fault network and are modulated by fluid-driven pore pressure changes, providing key insights into fault mechanics and post-seismic relaxation processes in carbonate environments.
本研究以2009年意大利拉奎拉地震序列为对象，探讨了控制余震分布的物理机制。通过分析断层带几何结构与地震活动性模式，研究表明余震的时空演化受断层带复杂结构与流体运移过程的共同控制。研究指出，地震活动空间分布反映了深部断层网络的复杂性，而流体扩散导致的孔隙压变化则调制了余震的时间演化。该成果为理解碳酸……

t: High-resolution earthquake relocation and spatial-temporal analysis of aftershocks combined with structural mapping to resolve fault-zone geometry and fluid diffusion pathways.
结合高精度地震重定位、余震时空分析与断层结构制图，解析断层带几何形态及流体扩散路径。
Seismic catalog and waveform data from the 2009 L'Aquila (Italy) earthquake sequence.

Aftershock distribution is highly controlled by fault-zone architecture, with fluid migration modulating the temporal evolution of seismicity along complex fault networks.

sum: This study investigates the 3D seismic structure and mantle flow dynamics beneath the curved Calabrian subduction zone in the Mediterranean. Using seismic travel-time tomography, the authors image the geometry of the subducting Calabrian slab and the surrounding mantle flow patterns. The results reveal complex mantle flow controlled by slab rollback and tearing, shedding light on the geodynamic evolution and formation mechanism of the highly curved Calabrian arc.
本研究利用地震走时层析成像技术，系统研究了地中海卡拉布里亚弯曲俯冲带的三维地震波速度与各向异性结构。研究揭示了俯冲卡拉布里亚板块的几何形态及其周围的地幔流模式，表明地幔流受到板块后撤和撕裂的强烈控制。这些发现为理解该地区高度弯曲弧形构造的形成机制与动力学演化提供了关键的深部地球物理证据。

Seismic arrival-time data from regional and teleseismic earthquakes recorded by stations in Italy and surrounding regions.

sum: This study investigates the 3D P-wave velocity structure down to 700 km depth beneath the Izu-Bonin-Mariana (IBM) subduction zone using seismic tomography. The results reveal distinct low-velocity anomalies representing deep mantle upwelling (DMU) triggered by devolatilization and melting of the subducted Pacific slab. Beneath the Izu-Bonin arc, the DMU tilts upward from the upper mantle bottom, whereas beneath the central Mariana Trough, it extends subvertically from the mantle transition zone. The authors propose that these distinct DMU morphologies control the different stages of arc rifting and back-arc spreading in the IBM system, providing crucial seismological evidence for deep-mantle-driven surface tectonics.

sum: This paper (Part I) presents a systematic analysis of newly-detected small seismic events in and near the Northern Korean Peninsula from 2004 to 2010. By applying waveform cross-correlation and template-matching techniques to regional seismic data, the authors identify previously uncataloged low-magnitude earthquakes and explosions. They perform high-precision relative relocation of these events, significantly improving the completeness and spatial resolution of the regional seismic catalog. This work helps delineate active fault structures and provides critical data for distinguishing between natural tectonic events and anthropogenic seismic sources in a geophysically and politically significant region.
本文（第一部分）系统分析了2004至2010年间朝鲜半岛北部及其周边新检测到的微小地震事件。作者利用波形互相关和模板匹配技术处理区域地震数据，识别出此前未被编目的低震级地震和爆炸事件。通过高精度相对重定位，显著提高了区域地震目录的完整性和空间分辨率。该研究有助于揭示活动断裂构造，并为区分该敏感区域的……

Successful detection of numerous small, previously uncataloged seismic events and high-precision relative locations that delineate fine-scale structures.

sum: This paper introduces a novel poromechanics-based framework for fully coupled reactive transport and geomechanics in porous rocks. By distinguishing the stress states of the host rock, pore fluid, and pore minerals, the framework rigorously models chemo-mechanical interactions during mineral precipitation and dissolution. Numerical examples demonstrate its ability to capture mineralization pressure and deformation while accounting for mineral compressibility. Compared to the eigenstrain method, this approach successfully models effective stress evolution and fracture development without requiring explicit microstructural geometry, making it highly suitable for reservoir-scale subsurface applications.
本文提出基于孔隙力学的多场耦合框架，模拟多孔岩石中化学运移与地质力学的完全耦合。该框架通过区分基岩、流体和矿物的应力状态，定量描述了矿物反应中的化学-力学相互作用。数值算例表明，该方法能有效捕捉矿化压力和形变。相比传统方法，它无需显式重建孔隙几何即可模拟有效应力演化和裂隙发育，适用于储层尺度分析。

t: A poromechanics-based framework that couples reactive transport and geomechanics by distinguishing stress states of host rock, pore fluid, and pore minerals.
基于孔隙力学的耦合框架，通过区分基岩、流体和矿物应力状态来耦合化学运移与地质力学。
Synthetic numerical examples simulating mineral precipitation/dissolution, mineralization pressure, and comparisons with the eigenstrain method.
模拟矿物沉淀/溶解、矿化压力的合成数值算例，以及与本征应变法的对比。
The framework successfully captures mineralization pressure, effective stress evolution, and fracture development without explicit pore geometry representation.
无需显式重建孔隙几何，成功捕捉了矿化压力、有效应力演化和裂隙发育。

sum: This study utilizes autonomous hydrophone records (2010–2022) to relocate 2,356 mid-ocean ridge earthquakes along the Southwest, Central, and Southeast Indian Ridges. By classifying segments into magmatic and tectonic types and propagating uncertainties via a Monte Carlo workflow, the authors calculate seismic moment budgets. They find that tectonic segments consistently release more seismic moment per unit length than magmatic ones. Relocated seismicity is tightly focused near the ridge axis (≤15 km) on the CIR and SEIR, but broader (≤30 km) on the SWIR. Fitting a tapered Gutenberg-Richter law reveals that coupled seismogenic thickness decreases from 1300 m to 70 m as spreading rate and magma supply increase. This supports a general model where mid-ocean ridge normal faulting is accommodated by a mix of seismic and aseismic slip modulated by local magma supply.

sum: This study presents NWCH, a new 3D anisotropic seismic wavespeed model of the lithosphere in Northwest China, western Mongolia, and eastern Kazakhstan. Using a simple isotropic starting model that honors lateral crustal thickness and topography variations, the author performs multiscale iterative full waveform inversion (FWI) on openly available broadband waveforms. The inversion progresses from 50–100 s down to 16 s over 8 stages and 105 iterations. NWCH significantly improves waveform fits compared to the starting model and existing 3D models (SinoScope1.0, SPiRaL). It successfully resolves regional features, including low-velocity sedimentary basins (Tarim, Junggar, Qaidam), the high-velocity Tarim Craton, and low-velocity crust/mantle beneath the Tibetan Plateau and Baikal Rift. The work highlights the efficacy of multiscale FWI starting from simplified models when honoring the crust-mantle interface.

sum: This paper introduces a spectral-domain pseudo-inverse construction method for linear inverse problems characterized by unitary diagonalizable matrices. By directly constructing a stable pseudo-inverse operator in the transform domain using the matrix's unitary diagonalization structure, the method avoids the high computational costs of traditional regularization or generalized inverse methods for large-scale problems. The author provides the analytic Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) for this class of matrices, defines spectral-domain regularization filtering factors, and proves the method's bounded stability and consistency in converging to the Moore-Penrose generalized inverse. Although numerically equivalent to zeroth-order Tikhonov regularization, this approach offers a distinct methodological path, revealing that stable generalized inverses can be directly constructed from spectral decomposition.

sum: The authors present the first 2D scattering and absorption maps of Metropolitan France in the 0.375–24 Hz frequency band. They employ a hybrid linearized inversion/grid-search scheme to separate source, site, and path effects from approximately 21,000 earthquake waveforms. Seismogram envelopes and their partial derivatives are modeled using Monte Carlo simulations of elastic radiative transfer, accounting for scattering anisotropy, P-S wave coupling, and crustal energy trapping. The attenuation parameters are then mapped tomographically using a least-squares algorithm with Tikhonov regularization. The resulting maps reveal strong spatial and frequency-dependent variations: scattering dominates at low frequencies (<1 Hz) particularly in sedimentary basins, while absorption dominates at higher frequencies, peaking in the western Pyrenees and French Alps. These high-resolution attenuation models are crucial for improving regional seismic hazard assessments.

sum: This paper presents a two-step inversion procedure based on elastic radiative transfer theory to separate earthquake source, path attenuation, and site amplification effects. In the first step, path effects are extracted from high-frequency (0.375–24 Hz) data envelopes. In the second step, a generalized inversion algorithm separates source and site terms, using reference stations with flat H/V ratios. Applied to ~21,000 waveforms in Metropolitan France, the method successfully estimates Mw, corner frequency, apparent stress, and stress drop for 1,279 events (ML 2.0–5.9). The study demonstrates that neglecting regional site effects (as in single-event schemes) or using inappropriate reference stations biases source parameter scaling, highlighting the necessity of rigorous site-effect correction for reliable source characterization.

sum: This comment evaluates the 67 teleseismic marsquake detections reported by Huang et al. (2025), which were identified using a deep learning phase picker on NASA's InSight seismic data. Dahmen et al. re-analyze these detections using complementary wind, pressure, and seismic polarization data. They find that all 67 reported events correspond to atmospheric noise, specifically small wind bursts misidentified as P-waves and subsequent larger bursts misidentified as S-waves. Furthermore, the authors show that the epicentral distances and magnitudes of these proposed events are physically inconsistent with known marsquake distributions. The study highlights the critical need to integrate environmental auxiliary data and physical constraints to avoid misinterpreting atmospheric and lander noise as genuine planetary seismic events.
本文对Huang等（2025）利用深度学习相位拾取器在NASA洞察号（InSight）地震数据中检测到的67个远震火星震进行了重新评估。作者结合风力、气压及地震信号极化特征进行分析，发现所有67个检测事件实际上都是大气噪声，即微弱风暴（被误判为P波）及随后的强风暴（被误判为S波）引起的地震响应。此外……

sum: This paper presents a prospectively specified reanalysis of published InSight RISE rotation products to evaluate their sensitivity to the Martian solid inner-core family proposed by Bi et al. (2025). Using three distinct analyses (forward detectability sweep, projection onto FICN-strength scans, and joint Bayesian confrontation), the author demonstrates that the non-detection of the Free Inner Core Nutation (FICN) in RISE data is uninformative. The proposed inner-core models are fully consistent with the published nutation-term perturbations because their predicted signatures fall below the current measurement noise floor. Consequently, the geodetic data neither support nor rule out the seismically proposed inner core, highlighting a sensitivity gap that requires future observational improvements to resolve.
对InSight RISE自转数据重新分析表明，其对地震学提出的火星固态内核不敏感。通过前向扫描、投影和贝叶斯评估，发现未探测到自由内核章动（FICN）并不能否定内核存在，因为其信号低于当前噪声下限。现有自转数据既不能证实也不能证伪火星内核，研究定量化了该敏感度差距。

sum: This study investigates the structural drivers of vertical uplift and exhumation in the western Nepal Himalaya. By integrating new and published cooling ages (apatite fission track, (U-Th)/He, and muscovite 40Ar/39Ar), basin accumulation data, and geomorphic uplift indicators, the authors evaluate variations in ramp geometry and kinematic sequences. They employ thermokinematic and landscape evolution modeling across three balanced cross-sections along the Simikot transect. The results demonstrate that the northern zone of high relief and young exhumation is driven by a combination of displacement over a mid-crustal ramp in the basal décollement and out-of-sequence faulting, resolving long-standing uncertainties regarding Himalayan uplift mechanisms.

sum: This study presents a novel method integrating infrared thermal imaging with numerical heat-conduction modeling to estimate coseismic temperatures on fault surfaces during laboratory earthquakes. By accounting for spatial resolution, experimental geometry, and real-to-nominal contact area ratios, the framework is applied to high-velocity rotary shear experiments on limestone. The results constrain the distribution of frictional heat sources, showing that flash heating was likely absent, and pointing to thermal softening or powder lubrication as the primary weakening mechanisms.

sum: This paper presents a theoretical 'two-interface driving model' for horizontal asthenospheric flow, utilizing an equivalent friction framework and an interface-selection principle. The model predicts a continuous velocity profile consisting of an upper drag layer (~30 km) and a return-flow zone (~150 km). It estimates effective friction coefficients at the lithosphere-asthenosphere boundary (LAB) and the mantle transition zone. Crucially, the model links macroscopic shear stress to microscopic olivine lattice-preferred orientation (LPO), predicting 3-D a-axis tilting testable by SKS splitting. Additionally, it unifies fluid, partial-melt, and solid friction by showing how melt fraction controls shear-creep thickness via grain size. This framework provides a physical mechanism for asthenospheric kinematics and seismic anisotropy.
本文提出软流圈水平流动的双界面驱动模型。基于等效摩擦框架和界面选择原理，预测了由上部拖拽层和回流区组成的连续速度剖面。模型将宏观剪切应力与微观橄榄石LPO联系起来，预测了可由SKS分裂检验的3D a轴倾角。此外，它通过熔体体积分数控制变形厚度，将流体、部分熔融和固体摩擦统一，为软流圈运动学和各向异性……

sum: This paper presents a continually learning neural-operator surrogate for three-dimensional airborne electromagnetic (AEM) Bayesian inversion. To overcome the extreme computational cost of 3D forward modeling in Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling, the authors train a neural operator that respects Maxwell's equations across consecutive geological priors. An ensemble-disagreement validity check routes out-of-distribution cases to the physics solver. Tested on the 2013 Capricorn TEMPEST survey in Western Australia, the surrogate successfully inverts over two million soundings in seconds while matching the full-solver posterior accuracy. This framework enables near real-time, survey-scale, uncertainty-quantified conductivity imaging.
本文提出一种用于三维航空电磁贝叶斯反演的持续学习神经算子代理模型。为解决MCMC采样中前向模拟计算慢的问题，该模型在连续地质先验中学习麦克斯韦定律，并利用集成不一致性检查分流异常样本。在西澳大利亚实际数据中，该方法在数秒内完成了超两百万个测点的反演，精度与全求解器一致，实现了大规模实时不确定性量化成……

sum: This paper introduces the Landslide Source-to-Inundation Process Model (LS-IPM), a reduced-complexity, process-based framework that reframes regional landslide debris hazard as a continuous, flux-based intensity problem rather than simulating discrete events. By coupling spatially distributed sediment production with mass-conservative, topography-controlled routing, LS-IPM evaluates hazard across entire landscapes. The authors apply the model at 25 m resolution to the ~25,000 km² West Coast region of New Zealand under present-day conditions, future climate scenarios (RCP6), and a Mw 8.0 Alpine Fault earthquake scenario. The results show high debris flux along steep slopes and convergent topography, with future climate conditions projected to increase mean annual debris flux by approximately 50%. This framework offers a scalable, geomorphologically constrained approach for regional hazard and probabilistic risk assessment.

sum: This study reanalyzes legacy passive seismic data across the Proterozoic Mount Isa Province in northern Australia using ambient noise tomography to construct a high-resolution 3-D crustal shear-wave velocity model. By integrating these results with reflection seismic profiles and surface geology, the authors identify distinct velocity contrasts across major crustal boundaries, such as the Gidyea Suture Zone. High-velocity anomalies at 5 km depth correspond to mapped upper-crustal intrusive bodies, which connect to broader high-velocity zones at 15–20 km depth. These features are interpreted as mafic intrusions from a trans-lithospheric magmatic system associated with regional metallogenic activity. The work demonstrates the value of integrating passive seismology with other geophysical datasets for mineral exploration.
本研究利用背景噪声成像构建了澳大利亚伊萨山省三维地壳剪切波速度模型。结合反射地震剖面，揭示了吉迪亚缝合带等主要地壳边界的速度对比。5 km深度的速度异常与上地壳侵入体对应，并与深部高速区相连，代表了与成矿相关的跨岩石圈岩浆系统中的基性侵入体。该研究展示了被动源地震学在成矿系统研究中的应用。

sum: This study utilizes detrital zircon U-Pb geochronology on dredged schists and sandstones from Bruce Bank and Discovery Bank in the southern Scotia Sea to constrain their tectonic provenance. Bruce Bank yielded Triassic schists (max sedimentation age ~216.2 Ma) correlating with the South Orkney accretionary complex. Sandstones from both banks and the South Orkney microcontinent yielded Permian-Triassic (258–224 Ma) and Cretaceous (140–110 Ma) maximum sedimentation ages. These findings suggest Bruce and Discovery banks were joined in the mid-Cretaceous and situated near the South Orkney Islands along the paleo-Pacific margin of Gondwana before undergoing Late Cretaceous-Cenozoic rifting and translation during the formation of the Scotia Sea.
本研究对南斯科舍海布鲁斯和发现海岭的疏浚样品进行碎屑锆石U-Pb定年。结果表明，布鲁斯海岭片岩最大沉积年龄为三叠纪（~216.2 Ma），与南奥克尼增生杂岩相当；两海岭砂岩具有二叠-三叠纪及白垩纪最大沉积年龄。这证实两海岭在白垩纪中期相连，并在裂解前位于冈瓦纳古太平洋边缘，为斯科舍海演化提供了关键约……

sum: This paper presents a hybrid inversion method combining Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Finite Element Modeling (FEM) to determine the geostress field of a pumped-storage power station. By using PSO to optimize XGBoost hyperparameters, the authors establish a high-precision non-linear proxy model that determines the optimal boundary conditions for the FEM. This approach effectively addresses non-linearity and discontinuity in deep geostress inversion. The method is applied to the Hongping pumped-storage power station in Jiangxi, China. The inversion results reveal that horizontal stress dominates at shallow depths, whereas vertical stress becomes dominant deeper down, showing strong agreement with in-situ measurements. This demonstrates the model's utility for underground engineering design and seismic hazard assessment.
本文提出结合PSO、XGBoost与有限元（FEM）的混合地应力反演方法。利用PSO优化XGBoost超参数构建高精度代理模型，确定有限元最佳边界条件，解决深部地应力反演的非线性问题。应用于江西洪屏抽水蓄能电站，结果表明浅部以水平应力为主，深部以垂直应力为主，与实测高度吻合，为地下工程设计提供了高精……

sum: This study analyzes CCTV video recordings of the 2026 Mw 6.8 Kumamoto and 2018 Mw 6.4 Hualien earthquakes to directly constrain fault slip-pulse characteristics. For the Kumamoto earthquake, the video resolves a 1.6-s slip pulse with a peak velocity of ~1.3 m/s, an estimated slip-weakening distance of ~0.7 m, and an average rupture speed of ~2.1 km/s. This short duration is remarkably similar to that of the much larger 2025 Mw 7.7 Myanmar earthquake, suggesting slip duration is controlled by local rupture geometry rather than magnitude alone. Conversely, the Hualien case demonstrates that distributed near-surface deformation can obscure slip-pulse signatures. The study highlights both the high potential and the limitations of optical video data for earthquake source physics.

sum: This study utilizes seismic data from the UPFLOW ocean-bottom seismometer (OBS) deployment to image the upper mantle and transition zone beneath the Azores-Canaries region. Using multimode waveform tomography, the authors identify widespread low-velocity anomalies and radial anisotropy variations between 230 and 400 km depth. These features indicate lateral spreading and ponding of eclogitic material from two neighboring thermochemical plumes. Crucially, where these lateral flows converge, fast-SV radial anisotropy suggests localized downwelling returning material to greater depths. This provides direct observational evidence of dynamic interactions and three-dimensional flow between adjacent mantle plumes, supporting geodynamic predictions of thermochemical plume behavior.

sum: The China–Western Australia Seismic Survey (CWAS), conducted from 2017 to 2019, deployed 56 broadband land stations along a 900 km transect and 8 ocean-bottom seismometers along a 500 km offshore line. This represents the first integrated land–ocean passive-source seismic array in northwestern Australia, aimed at overcoming thick sedimentary cover and sparse observations to image the region's Precambrian craton and passive-margin lithospheric structure. The dataset (FDSN network code 4N) is openly available. Example data products, including receiver functions, ambient-noise cross-correlations, and earthquake waveforms, demonstrate its high quality and suitability for crustal and lithospheric imaging. The newly documented offshore component extends coverage across the ocean–continent transition, providing a valuable resource for studying passive-margin evolution.

sum: This paper presents a Bayesian framework for seismic tomographic reconstruction and uncertainty quantification that incorporates geology-informed structural priors. Instead of conventional pixel-wise regularizations, the authors formulate explicit geological hypotheses using a Whittle-Matérn latent Gaussian field, truncated Karhunen-Loève expansion, and a differentiable nonlinear pushforward mapping to promote piecewise-constant velocity structures. This parameterization reduces dimensionality, enabling maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) sampling. The method is applied to ambient noise phase velocity tomography. Synthetic tests demonstrate accurate recovery of velocity contrasts and acquisition-related uncertainty patterns. Application to a ~1000-sensor dense array dataset yields structures consistent with prior geological assumptions and provides spatially resolved uncertainty estimates.

sum: This study constructs a high-resolution crustal strain rate model for the Southeastern Tibetan Plateau (SETP) using an expanded GNSS dataset of 997 vectors. The model reveals a prominent J-shaped high-strain zone along the Xianshuihe-Xiaojiang fault system (XXFS) extending 600 km southwestward. Combined with unsupervised Euler pole clustering machine learning, the results suggest a mid-to-lower crustal linkage between the XXFS and faults southwest of the Red River fault, indicating active fault propagation across this ancient boundary. The interior of the SETP exhibits widespread extensional deformation with clockwise rotation of principal axes and fault-bounded rotational domains. The strong correlation between high-strain zones and historical M >= 6 earthquakes provides a refined, physically-based framework for regional seismic hazard assessment.

sum: This study introduces DTSEC (DiTing Seismic Event Classifier), a model fine-tuned from a pretrained seismogram foundation model with over 100 million parameters to classify earthquakes, explosions, and collapses. DTSEC achieves an overall accuracy of 92.83% on the test set, showing superior sample efficiency by matching scratch-trained models using only 20% of the training data. To address regional performance drops, the authors apply joint fine-tuning with a small number of local samples from the Henan Seismic Network, China. This approach successfully adapts the model to local geological features while retaining global generalization. DTSEC offers a practical, deployable solution for seismic event classification, particularly in data-scarce regions.

sum: This study presents a fast, scalable, and differentiable machine-learning surrogate to approximate phase equilibrium predictions for mantle rocks under upper- to transition-zone conditions. Calibrated on a synthetic dataset of 2.0 million samples generated via Gibbs free energy minimization, the model predicts phase fractions and solid-solution compositions with high accuracy (uncertainties < 0.01 and 0.005 mol/mol, respectively). The GPU-accelerated surrogate achieves a speedup of four orders of magnitude compared to traditional thermodynamic minimizers. This acceleration, combined with differentiability, enables gradient-based sensitivity analysis of phase transitions to bulk chemistry, facilitating planetary-scale geodynamic modeling of seismic discontinuities and mantle convection.
本研究提出一种快速、可微的机器学习代理模型，用于预测上地幔至过渡带的岩石相平衡。模型基于200万个合成样本进行校准，预测相分数和固溶体成分的误差极低。该GPU加速模型比传统热力学计算快四个数量级，其可微性支持对化学成分变化的梯度分析，为行星尺度地幔对流和地震不连续面模拟提供了高效工具。

sum: This study addresses the limitation of ambient noise HVSR (HVSRN) at ocean-bottom seismometer (OBS) stations, which is typically unstable below 0.1 Hz due to oceanic noise. The authors propose using earthquake coda waves (HVSRC) from multiple events with long-duration coda (>=200 s) to obtain stable HVSR curves in the 0.05–10 Hz range. By inverting these curves using the 'hvgeneralized' algorithm under the diffuse field assumption, they construct 1D shear-wave velocity models down to ~10 km depth offshore Fukushima. The resulting models align with known sedimentary and crustal structures and successfully image a low-velocity zone associated with the Japan Trench plate interface at ~7 km depth. This demonstrates that HVSRC can effectively mitigate low-frequency instability in marine environments, extending HVSR applicability to deep crustal imaging.

sum: This study evaluates the robustness of geodetic source inversion at the Campi Flegrei caldera (Italy) during its 2007–2023 unrest. By repeating 3D heterogeneous numerical modeling with alternative multi-mission satellite datasets—including Sentinel-1, different COSMO-SkyMed processing, and GNSS measurements—the authors assess how data discrepancies affect subsurface source parameters. The results confirm a stable shallow inflating source at approximately 3.9 km depth and a deeper deflating reservoir, with consistent volume change estimates across different datasets. This work provides an explicit cross-validation of magma-driven deformation models, demonstrating that first-order geodetic constraints are highly reproducible and reliable for volcanic hazard assessment despite local data discrepancies.

sum: This study investigates the role of earthquake-induced progressive rock mass damage over late Pleistocene to Holocene timescales (past 25 ka) as a conditioning factor for modern landslides in the paraglacial Serpentine Valley, Alaska. Using distinct element numerical modeling, the authors simulate a simplified deglaciation sequence with 10 earthquakes under varying glacier thicknesses. The results show that while rigid glacier buttressing reduces co-seismic damage, it does not eliminate it. Topography, steep slopes, topographic convexity, and pre-existing joint networks exert primary control on new damage locations. The simulated damage patterns qualitatively match in situ structural and kinematic observations of active landslides in the valley. This conceptual study highlights how repeated seismicity over glacial timescales acts as a long-term conditioning process for paraglacial rock slope failures, with significant implications for modern landslide hazard assessments.

sum: This paper investigates the kinematics of the Sagaing fault system in Myanmar using GNSS geodetic observations. By analyzing crustal deformation and fault slip rates, the study provides insights into the strain accumulation and locking depth along different segments of the fault. The findings are used to discuss the seismic potential and implications for the 2025 Mw 7.7 Mandalay Earthquake, contributing to a better understanding of seismic hazards in this highly active strike-slip fault zone.

sum: This study evaluates legacy petrophysical logs and seismic reflection lines from the Vincent area in Iowa, USA, to explore geologic hydrogen occurrences within the Midcontinent Rift System (MRS). The authors identify hydrogen shows in the upper Eau Claire carbonate and map faults in the MRS basalts and overlying sedimentary strata that act as migration pathways. They demonstrate that obsolete neutron-gamma logging tools, when combined with resistivity, acoustic, and density logs, are sensitive to hydrogen accumulations. This work highlights the utility of legacy fossil fuel exploration data for modern green energy and geologic hydrogen exploration.

sum: This paper investigates the statistical properties of avalanches and interevent times in a sheared amorphous system using a field theoretical model of soft-glassy materials. By defining fluidity as the order parameter representing local plastic events, the authors demonstrate that both avalanche sizes and interevent times follow power-law distributions. Crucially, they establish a precise analytical relation between their scaling exponents. This theoretical framework successfully reproduces the stick-slip and avalanche behaviors observed across various amorphous systems, offering valuable physical insights into earthquake-like triggering and relaxation processes in disordered media.

sum: This paper investigates the performance of water versus supercritical carbon dioxide (ScCO2) as fracturing fluids in intact and jointed rocks. Using a 2D fully coupled hydromechanical finite-discrete element method (FDEM), the authors simulate fluid-driven fracturing under varying flow rates, in-situ stresses, and fluid viscosities. The results show that ScCO2 easily penetrates rock grains and joints, dilates them, and generates complex fracture branching and longer fractures compared to water. Additionally, ScCO2 requires lower breakdown pressures, offering a more efficient and environmentally friendly alternative for reservoir permeability enhancement while potentially mitigating the risks of induced seismicity associated with wastewater disposal.

sum: This computational study investigates how off-fault plasticity affects the propagation speed of elongated, width-limited strike-slip earthquake ruptures. Using a 2.5D width-averaged modeling approach combined with Mohr-Coulomb plasticity, the authors simulate rupture propagation in an inelastic medium. Unlike 2D models where off-fault dissipation grows indefinitely with rupture length, this model accounts for seismogenic width saturation. The simulations demonstrate that off-fault plastic deformation stabilizes ruptures into steady pulse-like propagation at speeds between 6.5% and 99% of the Rayleigh wave speed. This range matches observations of both typical earthquakes and slow tsunami earthquakes. The study systematically characterizes how rupture speed, pulse width, and peak slip velocity depend on initial fault stress, proximity to plastic failure, and seismogenic zone width, providing a viable mechanism for realistic rupture velocities on planar, homogeneous faults.

sum: This study introduces an artificial intelligence-driven modeling approach that integrates seismic hazard assessment to evaluate hydrocarbon trap evolution and reservoir pressure dynamics within the Zagros Lurestan Provinces. By combining machine learning algorithms with geological and geophysical datasets, the authors simulate the structural evolution of traps and estimate reservoir pressures under tectonic stress. The integration of seismic hazard parameters provides a novel way to assess reservoir integrity and risk, offering valuable insights for hydrocarbon exploration and structural geology in tectonically active fold-and-thrust belts.

sum: This Zenodo repository provides source code for generating synthetic Sdiff shear-wave splitting predictions and comparing them against observations. The package includes MATLAB scripts for elastic tensor preparation and AxiSEM3D input generation, a modified SplitRacer toolbox for automated Sdiff splitting measurements on synthetic seismograms, and Python analysis code. The Python tools compute mean squared error (MSE) misfit between observed and predicted splitting parameters, calculate cosine similarity to geodynamic strain patterns, perform hexagonal spatial binning, classify split/null measurements, and visualize geodynamic strain directions. It serves as a valuable tool for investigating deep-mantle anisotropy and core-mantle boundary dynamics.

sum: This paper presents a numerical modeling study investigating the effects of bulk poroelasticity on repeating earthquake sequences (RES). By coupling rate-and-state friction with poroelastic governing equations, the authors simulate the long-term behavior of fault slip and pore pressure evolution. The study reveals how bulk poroelastic deformation alters stress transfer, recurrence intervals, and nucleation processes of repeating events compared to purely elastic models. The key novelty lies in demonstrating the significant role of off-fault poroelastic coupling in modulating the timing and characteristics of seismic sequences.

sum: This paper proposes a perturbation-based implicit full-waveform inversion (IFWI) framework to address the slow convergence and poor deep-structure recovery of conventional IFWI. By decomposing the velocity model into a fixed background and a learnable neural network-parameterized perturbation, the method reduces multi-scale gradient interference. Additionally, a coordinate normalization strategy decouples spatial scale from the network's frequency response. Numerical experiments show that this approach improves convergence stability, structural resolution, and robustness to inaccurate initial models and missing low frequencies.

sum: This paper evaluates whether supervised machine learning models can outperform the standard coherence damage proxy (CDP) for earthquake damage mapping using Sentinel-1 SAR data. By combining Copernicus EMS damage grades with OpenStreetMap footprints across four earthquakes, the author tests logistic regression, gradient boosting, random forest, and SVM models at building, block, and grid cell scales. Under leave-one-area-out validation, gradient boosting models significantly outperform the CDP at the morphological block scale. For individual buildings, the improvement is marginal, while for grid cells, ML models do not beat the proxy. Interestingly, the robust logistic regression model relies heavily (79%-87%) on the spatial distribution and neighborhood of the coherence drop rather than just the mean drop, demonstrating the value of spatial context in SAR-based damage assessment.

sum: This study investigates the temporal changes of Earth's inner core surface beneath eastern South America from 2003 to 2024 using a repeating earthquake cluster. The authors show that extensive data contradictions challenge the hypothesis of inner core differential rotation. Instead, localized temporal changes of the inner core surface alone provide a simple and consistent explanation for the seismic observations. The mapped spatiotemporal evolution reveals that these surface changes are highly localized and exhibit irregular episodes of change, quiescence, and recovery. The study proposes two physical mechanisms: localized viscous deformation driven by episodic small-scale forces and localized alternate solidification/melting. These findings suggest that the inner core actively interacts with or influences small-scale driving forces of Earth's geodynamo on a timescale of years to days.
